prompt:
Build a comprehensive personal replacement for Wanderlog Pro in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, MapLibre GL, and user-supplied map and travel APIs.
The core loop is: build a collaborative trip itinerary from user-entered places, notes, and reservations, map them, and keep an offline copy.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
1. Itinerary Management: Create trips, days, places, reservations, notes, documents, packing items, and emergency contacts. The day timeline should support drag-and-drop reordering.
2. Mapping & Geocoding: Geocode user-entered places and display them through MapLibre. Implement cached trip-area tiles where allowed for offline viewing. Show routes between places and estimate travel times.
3. Automated Ingestion: Implement a feature to parse forwarded reservation text (flights, hotels, rental cars) locally into editable fields without logging message content, using a lightweight local NLP library or regex patterns.
4. Route Optimization: Add a tool to automatically optimize travel routes based on distance and travel time.
5. Offline Mode: Ensure the application functions without an internet connection using Service Workers and IndexedDB, syncing back to SQLite when online.
6. Export & Sharing: Export complete trip bundles as JSON, calendar files (ICS), Markdown, and PDF. Generate shareable, read-only links for friends.
7. Budget Tracking: Include a module to log expenses, categorize them, and split costs among travelers.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states. Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs. Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path. Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps. Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane. Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used. This should feel like a premium, snappy application.
